## What's new

Threadnote 5.3.0 brings reviewed updates for code-backed topic memories, background Gemma setup, and bundled development workflows.

### Review changes to maintained topics

Enroll a durable topic memory with its supporting code, and Threadnote can detect changes in the declared evidence and prepare an update with your selected local model. Inspect the evidence, edit the proposed text, and approve the exact document before it is saved. Revision checks, protected policies, provenance, and review history preserve the boundaries of accepted knowledge.

Private memories backed by one Obsidian note can also use this workflow. For code-backed topics, you can explicitly select supported one-hop code dependencies or configuration files to extend the evidence scope.

Topic maintenance remains experimental and opt-in in this stable release. Review every draft: usefulness on real topics, review effort, and general answer quality have not been established. Threadnote does not accept drafts or expand their evidence scope automatically.

### Prepare Gemma in the background

Eligible standalone installs and updates now download and verify the pinned Gemma 4 model in the background. Manager shows progress and recovery actions. Explicit provider and model choices stay intact; Gemma becomes the local default only when it is ready and you have not made a choice.

The download is approximately 4.6 GB, with memory and disk checks before it starts. Setup does not load the generation model or start a draft. Check progress with `threadnote models setup --status`, pause automatic setup with `threadnote models setup --auto off`, or retry with `threadnote models setup --retry`.

### Development workflows included

Threadnote now includes `dev-spec`, `dev-plan`, `dev-cycle`, and `watch-pr` for defining requirements, planning from current source, implementing and reviewing changes, and handling PR feedback. Supported agent setup installs them by default, and Threadnote updates refresh enabled installations while preserving edited files and opt-outs.

Use Manager's **Development workflows** page to preview and manage an installation, or start with `threadnote dev-skills list`. Installation makes the workflows available; it does not run them.

### Clearer reviews and memory previews

Topic and citation reviews have clearer evidence cards, quotations, status badges, and persistent actions. Draft generation shows activity, and a confirmed update immediately removes the resolved item and its counts.

Memory conflict reviews keep Preview and Confirm visible. Choosing “Both memories apply” for shared memories saves a local decision for the reviewed versions without editing or publishing either source.

Memory previews now render Mermaid diagrams. Projects with display names containing spaces and topics with sentence-style filenames also work more consistently across enrollment, review, and maintenance.

### More reliable project-scoped context

Graph refreshes and recall preserve the selected project scope through scheduling and indexing. Temporary graph reference resolution can proceed while another SQLite connection holds the main writer, reducing busy failures during concurrent graph work.
